name: Moral Machine: whom should a self-driving car spare?
author: Human Not Found
description: Original study: Awad, E., Dsouza, S., Kim, R., Schulz, J., Henrich, J., Shariff, A., Bonnefon, J.-F., & Rahwan, I. (2018). The Moral Machine experiment. Nature, 563(7729), 59-64. An online platform collected about 40 million decisions from millions of people in 233 countries and territories on dilemmas in which a self-driving car must kill one of two groups. Globally, people preferred to spare humans over animals, more lives over fewer and the young over the old; countries formed Western, Eastern and Southern clusters that weighed these preferences differently. This template gives ten participants nine dilemmas, each varying one attribute (species, number, age, gender, social status, fitness, lawfulness, intervention, passengers versus pedestrians), and runs three conditions whose participants live in the United States, Japan or Brazil, one country from each cluster. The original randomised every attribute of each scene and estimated effects with conjoint analysis; here each dilemma isolates one attribute and the option order alternates. Compare the share choosing each side per dilemma with the paper's Figure 2 and across conditions with its Figure 3. Participants are simulated: each is a Model participant, using the free test model until you choose a model, so the first runs only check the design; with the test model every participant takes the sample answer.

items.prompt: Staying kills 3 people crossing; swerving kills 3 dogs crossing in the other lane.
Staying kills 5 pedestrians; swerving kills 1 pedestrian.
Staying kills 2 children; swerving kills 2 elderly people.
Staying kills 2 women; swerving kills 2 men.
Staying kills 2 business executives; swerving kills 2 homeless people.
Staying kills 2 athletes; swerving kills 2 large, unfit people.
Staying kills 2 people crossing on a green signal; swerving kills 2 people crossing on a red signal.

options: Stay (spare those in the other lane)
items.prompt: Staying kills 2 pedestrians ahead; swerving kills 2 other pedestrians in the other lane.
Staying kills 3 pedestrians; swerving into a barrier kills the 3 passengers in the car.

config.prompt: A self-driving car with sudden brake failure will hit one of two groups. It can stay in its lane or swerve. For each case, choose which group the car should spare. Everyone else in the case dies.
